title: Configuration Management with Ansible
summary: Ansible automates the configuration of servers and deployment of applications without requiring agents. It connects over SSH, runs playbooks (YAML), and ensures servers match their desired state — idempotently. It's the dominant configuration management tool alongside Terraform.

sections.title: How Ansible works: agentless automation
sections.body:
Ansible manages remote machines over SSH (or WinRM on Windows). No agent is installed on targets — just Python. The control node (your machine or CI runner) pushes configuration.

```
Control Node (your machine)
│
├── ansible.cfg         — Ansible configuration
├── inventory/          — which hosts to manage
│   ├── hosts.ini
│   └── group_vars/
│       ├── all.yml
│       └── webservers.yml
├── playbooks/          — what to do
│   ├── deploy.yml
│   └── setup-server.yml
└── roles/              — reusable task collections
    ├── nginx/
    └── docker/
```

**Key concepts:**

```
Inventory     — the list of hosts Ansible manages
               (INI file, YAML, or dynamic from AWS/GCP)

Playbook      — YAML file defining a sequence of tasks to run
               one playbook can target multiple host groups

Task          — a single unit of work (install a package, copy a file)
               executed by a module

Module        — reusable unit of functionality
               (apt, yum, copy, template, service, docker_container)

Role          — reusable collection of tasks, variables, templates
               standard structure: tasks/, handlers/, templates/, defaults/

Handler       — a task triggered by notify, runs once at the end
               (restart nginx only if config changed)

Fact          — system information gathered by Ansible at runtime
               (ansible_os_family, ansible_memory_mb, ansible_default_ipv4)

Idempotency   — running a playbook twice produces the same result
               Ansible checks current state before making changes
```

**Install Ansible (on macOS/Linux):**

```bash
# pip (recommended — gets latest version)
pip3 install ansible

# macOS with homebrew
brew install ansible

# Verify
ansible --version
ansible-playbook --version
```

sections.title: Inventory: defining your infrastructure
sections.body:
The inventory tells Ansible which hosts to manage and how to group them.

**INI-format inventory:**

```ini
# inventory/hosts.ini

# Standalone hosts
bastion.example.com

# Groups
[webservers]
web1.example.com ansible_user=ubuntu
web2.example.com ansible_user=ubuntu

[databases]
db1.example.com ansible_user=ec2-user

[monitoring]
10.0.10.15 ansible_user=ubuntu ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/ops.pem

# Group of groups
[production:children]
webservers
databases

# Group variables
[webservers:vars]
http_port=80
max_clients=200
```

**YAML-format inventory (more expressive):**

```yaml
# inventory/hosts.yml
all:
  vars:
    ansible_user: ubuntu
    ansible_ssh_private_key_file: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
  children:
    webservers:
      hosts:
        web1.example.com:
          http_port: 80
        web2.example.com:
          http_port: 8080
    databases:
      hosts:
        db1.example.com:
          postgres_version: "15"
```

**Group variables (best practice — don't put vars in inventory):**

```yaml
# inventory/group_vars/all.yml — applies to every host
ansible_python_interpreter: /usr/bin/python3
app_name: my-platform
log_dir: /var/log/myapp

# inventory/group_vars/webservers.yml — applies to webservers group
nginx_version: "1.25"
ssl_cert_path: /etc/nginx/ssl

# inventory/host_vars/db1.example.com.yml — applies to one host
postgres_max_connections: 200
```

**Dynamic inventory (AWS example):**

```bash
# Install AWS dynamic inventory plugin
pip3 install boto3 botocore

# inventory/aws_ec2.yml
---
plugin: amazon.aws.aws_ec2
regions:
  - us-east-1
filters:
  instance-state-name: running
  tag:Environment: production
keyed_groups:
  - prefix: env
    key: tags.Environment
  - prefix: role
    key: tags.Role

# Test it
ansible-inventory -i inventory/aws_ec2.yml --list
ansible-inventory -i inventory/aws_ec2.yml --graph
```

**Useful inventory commands:**

```bash
# Test connectivity
ansible all -i inventory/hosts.ini -m ping
ansible webservers -i inventory/hosts.ini -m ping

# Run ad-hoc commands
ansible webservers -i inventory/hosts.ini -m command -a "uptime"
ansible all -i inventory/hosts.ini -m gather_facts --limit web1.example.com

# List all hosts in inventory
ansible-inventory -i inventory/hosts.ini --list
ansible-inventory -i inventory/hosts.ini --graph
```

sections.title: Playbooks: orchestrating server configuration
sections.body:
A playbook is a YAML file that defines tasks to run on hosts. Each play targets a group and runs tasks in order.

**Playbook structure:**

```yaml
# playbooks/setup-webserver.yml
---
- name: Configure web servers
  hosts: webservers        # from inventory
  become: true             # sudo (privilege escalation)
  vars:
    app_port: 8080
    deploy_user: deploy

  tasks:
    - name: Update apt cache
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        update_cache: yes
        cache_valid_time: 3600  # only update if >1 hour old

    - name: Install nginx
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: nginx
        state: present          # present=install, absent=remove, latest=upgrade

    - name: Install required packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name:
          - curl
          - git
          - htop
          - jq
        state: present

    - name: Create deploy user
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: "{{ deploy_user }}"
        shell: /bin/bash
        groups: docker
        append: yes

    - name: Copy nginx config
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: templates/nginx.conf.j2
        dest: /etc/nginx/conf.d/app.conf
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0644'
      notify: Restart nginx      # trigger handler

    - name: Ensure nginx is running
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: nginx
        state: started
        enabled: true            # start on boot

  handlers:
    - name: Restart nginx
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: nginx
        state: restarted
```

**Jinja2 templates:**

```nginx
# templates/nginx.conf.j2
server {
    listen {{ app_port }};
    server_name {{ ansible_hostname }};

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    }
}
```

**Conditionals, loops, and when:**

```yaml
- name: Install Docker on Ubuntu only
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: docker.io
    state: present
  when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"

- name: Install Docker on RHEL
  ansible.builtin.yum:
    name: docker
    state: present
  when: ansible_os_family == "RedHat"

- name: Create config directories
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "{{ item }}"
    state: directory
    mode: '0755'
  loop:
    - /etc/myapp
    - /var/log/myapp
    - /var/lib/myapp/data

- name: Copy multiple config files
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: "{{ item.src }}"
    dest: "{{ item.dest }}"
  loop:
    - { src: 'app.conf', dest: '/etc/myapp/app.conf' }
    - { src: 'logging.conf', dest: '/etc/myapp/logging.conf' }
```

**Register and debug:**

```yaml
- name: Check if service is running
  ansible.builtin.command: systemctl is-active nginx
  register: nginx_status
  ignore_errors: true

- name: Show nginx status
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "Nginx is {{ nginx_status.stdout }}"

- name: Start nginx only if stopped
  ansible.builtin.service:
    name: nginx
    state: started
  when: nginx_status.stdout != 'active'
```

**Run a playbook:**

```bash
# Dry run (check mode — no changes made)
ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.ini playbooks/setup-webserver.yml --check

# Show diff of what would change
ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.ini playbooks/setup-webserver.yml --diff

# Run for real
ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.ini playbooks/setup-webserver.yml

# Target specific hosts
ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.ini playbooks/setup-webserver.yml \
  --limit web1.example.com

# Run specific tags
ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.ini playbooks/setup-webserver.yml \
  --tags "nginx,config"

# Verbose output
ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.ini playbooks/setup-webserver.yml -v    # task output
ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.ini playbooks/setup-webserver.yml -vvv  # connection debug
```

sections.title: Roles: reusable configuration components
sections.body:
Roles are the standard way to organize Ansible code for reuse. A role bundles tasks, variables, templates, and handlers into a well-known directory structure.

**Role directory structure:**

```
roles/
└── nginx/
    ├── tasks/
    │   └── main.yml      ← entry point for tasks
    ├── handlers/
    │   └── main.yml      ← handlers triggered by notify
    ├── templates/
    │   └── nginx.conf.j2 ← Jinja2 templates
    ├── files/
    │   └── ssl.conf      ← static files to copy
    ├── vars/
    │   └── main.yml      ← vars that CANNOT be overridden
    ├── defaults/
    │   └── main.yml      ← default vars (CAN be overridden)
    └── meta/
        └── main.yml      ← role metadata, dependencies
```

**Create a role with ansible-galaxy:**

```bash
# Scaffold a role
ansible-galaxy role init roles/nginx
ansible-galaxy role init roles/docker
ansible-galaxy role init roles/app-deploy
```

**Example role: docker installer**

```yaml
# roles/docker/defaults/main.yml
docker_version: "24.0"
docker_users: []          # list of users to add to docker group
docker_compose: true      # install docker compose plugin

# roles/docker/tasks/main.yml
---
- name: Install prerequisites
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - apt-transport-https
      - ca-certificates
      - curl
      - gnupg
    state: present
    update_cache: yes

- name: Add Docker GPG key
  ansible.builtin.apt_key:
    url: https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg
    state: present

- name: Add Docker repository
  ansible.builtin.apt_repository:
    repo: "deb [arch=amd64] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu {{ ansible_distribution_release }} stable"
    state: present

- name: Install Docker
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - docker-ce
      - docker-ce-cli
      - containerd.io
    state: present
  notify: Start Docker

- name: Add users to docker group
  ansible.builtin.user:
    name: "{{ item }}"
    groups: docker
    append: yes
  loop: "{{ docker_users }}"
  when: docker_users | length > 0

# roles/docker/handlers/main.yml
---
- name: Start Docker
  ansible.builtin.service:
    name: docker
    state: started
    enabled: true
```

**Using roles in a playbook:**

```yaml
# playbooks/provision-server.yml
---
- name: Provision web servers
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  vars:
    docker_users:
      - ubuntu
      - deploy

  roles:
    - role: docker
    - role: nginx
      vars:
        nginx_port: 443
    - role: app-deploy

# Or use include_role for conditional loading:
  tasks:
    - name: Install Docker
      ansible.builtin.include_role:
        name: docker
      when: install_docker | default(true)
```

**Ansible Galaxy: installing community roles:**

```bash
# Install a community role
ansible-galaxy role install geerlingguy.docker
ansible-galaxy role install geerlingguy.nginx

# requirements.yml — pin versions for reproducibility
# roles:
#   - name: geerlingguy.docker
#     version: 7.1.0
#   - name: geerlingguy.nginx
#     version: 3.2.0

ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yml

# Collections (newer packaging format with modules + roles + plugins)
ansible-galaxy collection install amazon.aws
ansible-galaxy collection install kubernetes.core
```

sections.title: Exercise: write a playbook to configure the sandbox
sections.body:
Practice Ansible patterns against localhost — no remote hosts needed. The sandbox terminal works perfectly for this.

```bash
# 1. Install Ansible
pip3 install ansible --quiet
ansible --version

# 2. Create a local inventory pointing at localhost
mkdir -p /workspace/ansible-lab && cd /workspace/ansible-lab

cat > inventory.ini << 'EOF'
[local]
localhost ansible_connection=local ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3
EOF

# Test connectivity
ansible local -i inventory.ini -m ping
# Expected: localhost | SUCCESS => {"ping": "pong"}

# 3. Gather facts about this machine
ansible local -i inventory.ini -m gather_facts | head -80
# Shows: OS, memory, CPU, IP, etc. — this is what Ansible knows automatically

# 4. Write a playbook
cat > setup-tools.yml << 'EOF'
---
- name: Set up dev tools
  hosts: local
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    tools:
      - curl
      - jq
      - htop
    workspace_dir: /workspace/ansible-lab/output

  tasks:
    - name: Show OS info
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "Running on {{ ansible_distribution }} {{ ansible_distribution_version }}"

    - name: Show available memory
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "Memory: {{ ansible_memtotal_mb }}MB total, {{ ansible_memfree_mb }}MB free"

    - name: Create workspace directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ workspace_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Write system info to file
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          hostname: {{ ansible_hostname }}
          os: {{ ansible_distribution }} {{ ansible_distribution_version }}
          kernel: {{ ansible_kernel }}
          memory_mb: {{ ansible_memtotal_mb }}
          cpu_count: {{ ansible_processor_count }}
          python: {{ ansible_python_version }}
          timestamp: {{ ansible_date_time.iso8601 }}
        dest: "{{ workspace_dir }}/system-info.txt"

    - name: Read back the file
      ansible.builtin.command: cat {{ workspace_dir }}/system-info.txt
      register: info_output
      changed_when: false

    - name: Display file contents
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "{{ info_output.stdout_lines }}"
EOF

# 5. Dry run first
ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini setup-tools.yml --check

# 6. Run it
ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini setup-tools.yml

# 7. Verify output
cat /workspace/ansible-lab/output/system-info.txt

# 8. Run again — notice all tasks show 'ok' not 'changed' (idempotency)
ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini setup-tools.yml

# 9. Explore Kubernetes facts from inside the sandbox
# Ansible can also run kubectl commands and register results:
ansible local -i inventory.ini -m command -a "kubectl get nodes -o wide"
ansible local -i inventory.ini -m command -a "kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Running"
```
